title: Flowable's documentation named the technical-versus-business audit distinction before we did
content:
The Flowable reference reads: *"Flowable creates a technical audit trail (history) by default. When it is required to have a business audit trail, the audit task is the easiest way to do this."*

That sentence draws exactly the distinction an external decision-record layer is built on — execution history is not a record of decisions — and it appears in the vendor's own documentation rather than in a competitor's analysis.

Two implications follow. The distinction is legible to buyers in this category, so it does not need teaching, which lowers the cost of every conversation about it. And a vendor articulate enough to name the gap is likely to close it, which is what happened. Finding your thesis stated in a vendor's docs is simultaneously validation and a warning.
description: Its own reference states that the engine creates a technical audit trail by default and that a business audit trail requires the audit task — the vendor articulated the gap and then filled it.
